summary: Gives instructions to IANA for creating a new registry of codepoints for the flags field in the Session Attribute object of RSVP-TE signaling messages. These are used in MPLS and Generalized MPLS. It is an informational document.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 4859 creates a registry for the flag bits in RSVP-TE Session Attribute objects. The list records existing uses and sets IETF consensus as the rule for assigning new flags.

how to request a new rsvp-te flag
what is the rsvp-te session attribute flags registry
subtitle: Creates a registry for flags in the RSVP-TE Session Attribute object.

tldr.problem: Different RFCs had assigned uses to bits in the RSVP-TE Session Attribute flags field, creating a need to track assignments centrally.
tldr.mechanism: IANA created the Session Attribute Object Flags registry under RSVP-TE Parameters; new flags may be assigned only by IETF consensus.
tldr.outcome: RFC 4859 is Informational and records the existing flag uses without defining the procedures for those flags.

today: RFC 4859 is Informational. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: The Session Attribute Flags
sections.content: The RSVP-TE Session Attribute object, carried in an RSVP Path message, contains an eight-bit flags field. RFC 3209 assigned uses to three bits, and later MPLS and GMPLS RFCs assigned additional bits. RFC 4859 lists existing uses and creates a registry to avoid assigning a bit more than once.
sections.plainLanguage: The Session Attribute object has eight flag bits, with uses assigned in several documents. The registry records those assignments so a bit is not reused accidentally.

sections.title: Existing Uses and New Assignments
sections.content: The RFC records six existing flag values: 0x01 for local protection, 0x02 for label recording, 0x04 for SE Style, 0x08 for bandwidth protection, 0x10 for node protection, and 0x20 for a path re-evaluation request. These uses are defined by RFCs 3209, 4090, and 4736. New flags may only be assigned by IETF consensus.
sections.plainLanguage: The initial registry lists six flags and the RFC that defined each use. IETF consensus is required to assign another flag.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: RFC 4859 says the registry helps protect the IETF process against denial-of-service attacks. Apart from that point, it states that there are no security considerations for the document.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC says the registry helps protect the IETF process. It identifies no other security considerations.
